culturalEntries.title: Kazhugumalai Vettuvan Koil and Jain Beds
culturalEntries.titleTa: கழுகுமலை வெட்டுவான் கோயில் மற்றும் சமணர் படுக்கைகள்
culturalEntries.shortDescription: An 8th-century monolithic Pandya temple carved top-down from a single rock, accompanied by extensive rock-cut Jain bas-reliefs.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Kazhugumalai is a remarkable archaeological site showcasing early Pandya rock-cut architecture. The centerpiece is the 'Vettuvan Koil' (Temple of the Slayer), an unfinished monolithic Shiva temple carved entirely from the top down into a solid granite hillside, drawing comparisons to Ellora's Kailasanatha temple. Just steps away are over 100 exquisite Jain rock-cut sculptures and stone beds dating back to the 8th and 9th centuries, highlighting a period of profound religious coexistence and artisanal mastery.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Commissioned by Pandya kings in the 8th century CE.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A rare architectural marvel demonstrating the 'top-down' monolithic carving technique in South India, while serving as a vital record of Jainism's influence in the Pandya kingdom.
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: State Archaeological and Historical Documentation; Tamil Nadu Tourism

chatbotKnowledge.keywords: thoothukudi, kazhugumalai, vettuvan koil, jain beds, monolithic, pandya, rock cut
chatbotKnowledge.answerEn: Kazhugumalai in Thoothukudi district features the Vettuvan Koil, an 8th-century unfinished monolithic Shiva temple carved top-down from a single rock by the Pandyas, along with exquisite rock-cut Jain sculptures.
chatbotKnowledge.answerTa: தூத்துக்குடி மாவட்டத்தில் உள்ள கழுகுமலையில், பாண்டியர்களால் மலையை மேலிருந்து கீழாகக் குடைந்து உருவாக்கப்பட்ட 8-ஆம் நூற்றாண்டு ஒற்றைக்கல் சிவன்கோயிலான வெட்டுவான் கோயிலும், எண்ணற்ற சமணச் சிற்பங்களும் அமைந்துள்ளன.
